Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon). NxLabs Phase 1 shipped (commit `2fe13e0632`) — a real, working mod catalog with genuine backend data (verified Modrinth license/downloads/game-versions, "Recommended Server" sizing, "no matching server yet, order one" messaging, admin support-status toggle). The functional core is solid and must NOT be regressed. The owner has now seen it live and given detailed, specific feedback — this brief supersedes any earlier, narrower one.

## Read these 8 real design mockups FIRST, literally — they are the approved direction, not inspiration
Already saved at `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/`: `logo.png` (the real NxLabs logo — NX in Nxeon's blue-purple gradient + flask + "LABS" wordmark, use this actual file), `hero-collage.png` (finished multi-game hero background art, use this actual file), `marketing-home.png`, `portal-home.png`, `game-page-marketing.png`, `game-page-portal.png`, `mod-page-marketing.png`, `mod-page-portal.png`. Read every one of these image files directly before writing code. Match palette, spacing, card composition, and section order precisely.

## Everything the owner has flagged as wrong or missing — fix ALL of it, this is not partial scope

**1. No real portal/marketing separation.** Clicking a mod on the logged-in portal (`/dashboard/nxlabs`) currently navigates to the public marketing mod page. Build genuinely separate portal-chrome'd game-detail and mod-detail routes (matching `game-page-portal.png`/`mod-page-portal.png` — portal's own sidebar/nav, not marketing nav), and fix the portal browse page's links to point at them.

**2. "These screens look terrible" — visual quality gap.** The shipped mod page is a bare text list (small square icon, plain "Details" list, letter-avatar "related mods" cards) next to the rich mockups. Rebuild marketing-home, portal-home, marketing/portal game-detail, and marketing/portal mod-detail to match the mockups' actual visual richness: real hero art, real card compositions, real iconography — not a functional-but-bare skeleton.

**3. No real gallery/screenshot images, mod logos, or textures shown.** This is a DATA gap, not just a UI gap: check `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` (built in Phase 1) — it likely only fetches Modrinth's `icon_url` and nothing else. Modrinth's real API (`GET /v2/project/{id}`) also returns a `gallery[]` array — each item `{url, raw_url, featured, title, description, ordering}` — CDN-hosted, hotlinkable, no auth needed. Extend the verify script to fetch and store gallery image URLs (add a schema field if `GameMod` doesn't have one, e.g. `galleryUrls String[]`, following this codebase's established `String[]`-not-a-join-table convention for simple lists — check how similar array fields are already modeled elsewhere first). Re-run the script against production so real mods actually get real gallery images. Render this gallery on the mod detail page (the image-gallery strip shown in `mod-page-marketing.png`/`mod-page-portal.png`). For resourcepack/shader/texture-pack project types specifically, the gallery IS the primary content — make sure those get proper visual treatment, not an afterthought.

**4. No visible author, total downloads prominently shown.** Check whether `GameMod` already captures an author/creator name from Modrinth's project data (the project record includes a `team`/author info — Modrinth's API may need a small additional call to resolve the display name, e.g. `GET /v2/team/{id}/members`). If missing, add it via the verify script, store it, and display it prominently (avatar + name + follow-style UI per the mockup, even if "follow" doesn't do anything real yet — clearly label it non-functional rather than fake the interaction, or omit the button entirely and just show the name/avatar). Total downloads must be a real number from Modrinth's `downloads` field, shown prominently, not buried.

**5. No ratings or comments — build a REAL, minimal system, do not fake or omit it.** This is genuinely new scope (confirmed by prior research: nothing like this existed before). Add real schema (new models, e.g. `ModRating` and `ModComment` — check `prisma/schema.prisma`'s existing conventions: cuid ids, `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, a real `userId` FK to `User`, following the exact id/timestamp/relation conventions already used throughout this schema, NOT copying the existing admin-only `Review` model which has no `userId` at all — this must be genuinely user-authored). Minimum viable version: an authenticated user can leave one star rating (1-5) and optionally a text comment per mod; the mod page shows a real aggregate average + real count (computed from actual `ModRating` rows, not fabricated) and a real, paginated comment list. Include basic abuse resistance (one rating per user per mod — a unique constraint on `(userId, gameModId)` — and a simple length cap on comment text) but do not over-build moderation tooling in this pass; a simple admin-can-delete-a-comment action reusing the existing `requireAdmin()`/`recordAudit()` pattern is enough. Do NOT show fake star ratings or fake review counts anywhere — every rating/count displayed must trace to a real row.

**6. Search bar.** Add a real, working search input on both the marketing browse/catalog pages and the portal browse page, querying the real `GameMod` table (name, game family, category — a simple `contains`/`ILIKE`-style filter is fine, this doesn't need full-text search infrastructure) and updating the results grid live or on submit — your call on exact UX, but it must actually filter real data, not be a decorative input that does nothing.

**7. "Proper segregation for all the different games."** Don't just have one flat catalog with a filter-chip row bolted on. Build real per-game landing pages (matching `game-page-marketing.png`/`game-page-portal.png`) for every game family that has catalog entries — each with its own hero, its own category tabs (Mods/Plugins/Shaders/Texture Packs/Maps/Modpacks as relevant to that game), and its own featured-mods grid scoped to that game. The catalog browse pages should link into these, and the "Browse Games"/"Popular Games" lists in the mockups should route here. Reuse `gameArt()`/`GAME_ART_SLUG` (`lib/nx/catalog.ts`/`lib/games.ts`) and the `/public/games/` art already used by the `/game-servers` cover carousel for each game's real hero/icon art — do not leave any game with a broken/missing image.

**8. Real assets already in hand.** Place `logo.png` as `/public/nxlabs/logo.png` and `hero-collage.png` as a real static asset, and use them in both nav bars / the marketing hero. Replace whatever placeholder branding Phase 1 shipped.

**9. Icon/badge already fixed, don't touch it.** `lib/nx/nav.ts`'s NxLabs entry now uses a real `beaker` icon (added to `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`) and a `badge: "MOD STORE"` — this already shipped in commit `7abc7e8b60`, on top of Phase 1. Leave this alone, just make sure the portal shell you build honors it.

## What to explicitly NOT fake
No invented review counts, star ratings, download numbers, or author names anywhere. If a specific real data point genuinely isn't available for a given mod (e.g. Modrinth doesn't expose something), omit that field gracefully for that mod rather than inventing a placeholder number. This app-wide discipline (real numbers or honest omission) has been enforced everywhere else this session — NxLabs is not an exception.

## Process
1. Read `lib/nx/nav.ts`, `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`'s nav array, and the real portal shell component (check `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GamePanelShell.tsx` or wherever NxLabs' own portal chrome currently lives) before building new chrome — reuse the established shell pattern.
2. Read what Phase 1 actually built in full before changing it: the public catalog pages under `app/(marketing)/`, `/dashboard/nxlabs` and its components, `lib/actions-mods.ts`, `GameMod`/`ServerMod` in `prisma/schema.prisma`, `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
4. Real browser verification (Playwright, desktop + mobile): marketing home, portal home (logged in), a marketing game page, a portal game page, a marketing mod page with a real gallery + real rating/comment section, a portal mod page, and the search bar actually filtering results on both marketing and portal. Screenshot each against its mockup.
5. Check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule — don't build directly in /opt/nxeon.
6. Credential hygiene: DB reads/writes via `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run via `npx tsx`. Never print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` string — leaked the production DB password multiple times already this session.
7. Deploy: commit → push → `deploy-staging.sh` → verify 200 → `promote-production.sh` → verify 200 and a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (record `cat /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID` first, current value should be from commit `7abc7e8b60`). Other agents may be concurrently active in this repo — if a deploy collides, retry once after confirming staging is healthy, never revert someone else's work. Run `npx tsx prisma/seed-gamemods.ts` and the verify script against production DB after any schema change, same as Phase 1 did.

Report back: every schema addition (ratings/comments/gallery/author), real numbers from a live re-verify run (how many mods now have real gallery images, real author names), confirmation the portal/marketing split is genuinely two routes, confirmation search actually filters real data on both sides, confirmation per-game pages exist for every catalogued game family with working art, screenshot-level comparison against each mockup noting any deliberate deviation, and the production deploy confirmation with fresh BUILD_ID.
